name: Back pain
description: Loose ligaments, hormonal changes, and a growing belly are usually behind the pain. Walking, yoga, and a good pillow go a long way.

name: Bloating & gas
description: Bloating, burping, unbuttoned pants – progesterone slows digestion down. Small, frequent meals can ease it.

name: Breast leaking
description: That's colostrum, aka your baby's first food. Your body starts making it during pregnancy, and it's normal to leak a bit before birth.

name: Breast soreness
description: Growth, soreness, leaking, lumps – all normal, and all to prep your body to nurse your baby.

name: Constipation
description: An increase in the hormone progesterone, which slows the digestive tract, is one culprit behind pregnancy constipation.

name: Contractions
description: Braxton Hicks contractions, or practice contractions before labor, usually start in the second or third trimesters.

name: Cramping
description: Warm baths, fluids, moving around, lying down, and bending toward the pain are ways to relieve pregnancy cramping.

name: Dizzy & lightheaded
description: Dizziness during pregnancy is caused by changes in your heart rate and the amount of blood your system is pumping.

name: Fatigue
description: Fatigue is most common in the first and third trimesters. Symptoms that interrupt sleep and hormones are behind it.

name: Food aversions
description: Pickles at midnight? The thought of chicken making you gag? Blame surging hormones, which are rewiring your sense of taste and smell.

name: Food cravings
description: Between 50 and 90% of women have at least one food craving during pregnancy. Here are some common ones.

name: Frequent urination
description: The frequent need to pee is caused by hormonal changes and your growing uterus pushing on your bladder.

name: Headaches
description: Warm showers, cold or warm compresses, acetaminophen and drinking enough fluids are ways to treat pregnancy headaches.

name: Heartburn & indigestion
description: You can relieve heartburn during pregnancy by eating small meals, drinking water and chewing gum after eating.

name: Itching
description: Itching, caused by stretching and drier skin during pregnancy, is common, affecting about 20% of pregnant women.

name: Mood changes
description: Surging estrogen and progesterone can leave you anxious one minute and elated the next. It can feel like a lot!

name: Nausea
description: Up to 70% of moms-to-be experience nausea and vomiting (also known as morning sickness). Surging hormones are mostly to blame.

name: Pelvic pain
description: The hormone relaxin loosens your pelvic ligaments to prep for birth. That extra movement can cause anything from a dull ache to a sharp stab.

name: Shortness of breath
description: No wonder you're winded: Your growing uterus is crowding your lungs, your blood volume is up, and you're literally breathing for two.

name: Skin, hair & nail changes
description: Surging hormones and your changing body can cause skin issues like stretch marks, acne, varicose veins, and melasma.

name: Sleep issues
description: Insomnia, restless legs, weird dreams, a bladder with zero chill – pregnancy makes quality sleep hard to come by.

name: Spotting
description: Light bleeding or spotting is normal early in pregnancy, but check with your doctor or midwife to be sure.

name: Strong sense of smell
description: A super-powered sense of smell affects about two-thirds of pregnancies, with surging hormones most likely to blame.

name: Stuffy nose
description: Stuffed up? Congestion is a common pregnancy symptom that happens when hormone surges cause nasal passages to swell.

name: Sweating
description: Running warmer than usual? Totally normal. Pregnancy boosts your blood flow, which can leave your skin feeling extra warm.

name: Swelling
description: Remedies for pregnancy swelling include drinking plenty of fluids, putting your feet up, and wearing compression socks.

name: Vaginal discharge
description: Vaginal discharge increases during pregnancy because your body is producing more estrogen.

name: Vomiting
description: Throwing up in pregnancy? You're not alone. Vomiting often kicks in around week 6, probably thanks to a surge in pregnancy hormones.

name: Other
description: Not every symptom has a neat label. Log what you're experiencing and talk to your provider if you need help making sense of it.
